findings.quote: Making the convention explicit restores the ceiling.
findings.issue: This is a causal claim drawn from confounded pairs with n=3 per arm, and one of the pairs is misidentified. (1) RH-OCFLB-CHART-01-ADAPTER changes more than the contract when set against LB-CHART-01-ADAPTER. Its gold has a visible unary minus (`-drift.getX() * explodePercent`) where LB-CHART-01-ADAPTER has a quiet `+ offset.getX()`. Its definer reads forward (`point2 - point1`) where the LB definer reads backwards (`point1 - point2`). The names and the chain also differ. A self-incriminating gold and the absence of an odd-looking competitor are exactly the factors MECHANISM_MINING.md names as the strongest predictors of recovery. (2) CF-V3 is not the 'explicit-contract twin of CF-V1'. CF-V3 is ADV-DEFINER-01 plus a definer javadoc; its test patch is identical and only the drift javadoc differs. CF-V1 adds the `retreat` second caller and its test, which CF-V3 lacks. CF-V1's only miss was ENTRY_POINT (getArcBounds), not a convention attribution, so CF-V3 does not address it. (3) CF-V5 does not make a convention explicit: it adds a visible operator at the gold and flips the definer. (4) CF-V3 states the contract on the definer, not 'at the gold'. (5) ocflb-v1 was a Claude result under a protocol that did not allow test execution. The differences are 1/3 vs 3/3 (Fisher two-sided p=0.40) and 2/3 vs 3/3 (p=1.0).

With 3 runs per arm, and with the OCFLB variant also adding a visible operator at the gold and a forward-reading definer, this is consistent with the earlier ocflb-v1 (Claude) result. findings.issue: This is a causal generalisation that the design does not support. (1) All 12 S1 misses were on re-hosted adversarial instances tuned against Claude. Every freshly built instance was at ceiling whatever its mechanism: S2 36/36, held-out 43/43 answered, Phase 4 6/6. So 'fresh build' is fully confounded with 'single defensible owner'. (2) P4-COMPRESS07-r1 changed no documentation; it only removed the sibling and its test. The blind labels already judged the parent's docs to make the gold the owner (defensible = no x3), so it is not an instance where the documentation newly leaves a single owner. (3) X4 says Phase 4 revisions are diagnostics that are 'never confirmation evidence', yet they are pooled here with the held-out runs. (4) One model at effort medium, 9 held-out instances and 0/43 errors: the Wilson 95% upper bound on the error rate is about 0.08, which is not 'disappear'.

Their taxonomy reuses, verbatim, the coordinator's category names coined from these same 12 runs (ENTRY_POINT_RANKING, DECOY_DOC_CONTRADICTION, CONVENTION_ATTRIBUTION, MASK_PLACEMENT_ATTRIBUTION).
